findings.evidence: REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(COALESCE(u, '')), '[^a-zµ]', '', 'g') collapses 'mg/mL' to 'mgml'; no entry in the CASE map for 'mgml'. Same fate for 'g/100ml', etc.
findings.recommendation: Parse compound units by splitting on '/' or other delimiters and returning a valid factor (e.g., 'mg/mL' means 1 mg per 1 mL, so factor is 1 if the view handles volume separately). Alternatively, add explicit mappings for common per-volume units.

findings.title: Hard-coded 18-hour window constant in workout-sleep gap calculation
findings.description: The maximum gap between a workout and a sleep onset is defined as `18 * 60 * 60 * 1000` directly in code with a descriptive variable name but no named constant.
findings.evidence: `const eighteenHrMs = 18 * 60 * 60 * 1000;`
findings.recommendation: Define a named constant (e.g., `WORKOUT_SLEEP_GAP_MAX_MS`) at the top of the file to make the intent explicit and allow easy adjustment.

findings.title: Distance conversion left solely to display layer
findings.description: Query functions such as `getActivities` return distance in meters without converting to miles; any consuming chart must call `formatDistance` or use `METERS_PER_MILE`. While centralization minimizes risk, a new chart could omit the conversion and display meters as miles.
findings.evidence: The comment in format.ts states 'format.ts is the canonical formatter' and queries.ts exports raw metrics; no `distance_miles` field is added at the query layer.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a precomputed `distance_miles` column in the query layer (or a transform wrapper) so that all consumers receive a miles value by default, reducing drift risk.

findings.title: Lack of NaN guard after Number() conversion in getWhoopCaloriesBurnt
findings.description: The function calls `Number(c.kilojoule)` and then `kjToKcal(kj)`. If `kilojoule` is a non-numeric string (e.g., 'NaN', 'N/A'), `Number()` returns NaN, which propagates through `kjToKcal` and into `Math.round`, producing NaN. There is no `isNaN` check after the Number conversion.
findings.evidence: `const kj = Number(c.kilojoule); const kcalExact = kjToKcal(kj);` with no `isNaN(kj)` guard. The earlier check `c.kilojoule == null` only catches null/undefined.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (isNaN(kj)) continue;` after the Number conversion to skip malformed rows.

findings.title: Silent duplicate-cycle overwrite in getWhoopCaloriesBurnt
findings.description: When two WHOOP cycles map to the same calendar date (rare but possible), the last-write-wins logic of `byDate.set` silently overwrites the earlier entry. No warning or decision log is emitted.
findings.evidence: `byDate.set(calendar_date, { ... })` without checking whether a value already exists for the key.
findings.recommendation: Log a warning when overwriting, and consider selecting the cycle with the more complete dataset (e.g., non-zero kJ) or averaging if both are valid.

findings.title: `unit_to_mg_factor` silently drops rows for unrecognized and compound units
findings.description: The SQL function `pds.unit_to_mg_factor` returns `NULL` for unrecognized units like `IU`, `oz`, `mL`, `drops`, `scoops`, and `capsules`. Because it uses `REGEXP_REPLACE` to strip non-alphabetic characters, compound units like `mg/mL` are collapsed to `mgml` and also fall through to `NULL`. This causes the `supplement_intake_by_compound` rollup view to silently drop these rows, leading to underreported supplement intake.
findings.evidence: The `CASE` statement only handles variations of mg, g, mcg, and kg. The regex `[^a-zµ]` removes the slash in `mg/mL`.
findings.recommendation: Add support for common units like `IU` (with compound-specific conversion factors if necessary, or pass them through un-converted if they can't be normalized to mg). Fix the regex to handle or preserve slashes for compound units like `mg/mL`, or add `mgml` to the `CASE` statement. Log or store a fallback for unrecognized units instead of silently returning `NULL`.

findings.title: `formatDuration` truncates instead of rounding to the nearest minute
findings.description: The `formatDuration` function uses `Math.floor` for both hours and minutes. This means that a duration of 3599 seconds (59 minutes and 59 seconds) will be formatted as `59m` instead of `1h 0m`. Similarly, 59 seconds will be formatted as `0m`. This truncation can lead to slightly unintuitive display values compared to standard rounding.
findings.evidence: `const h = Math.floor(seconds / 3600); const m = Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60);`
findings.recommendation: Use `Math.round(seconds / 60)` to get the total minutes, then calculate hours and minutes from that rounded total to ensure durations are rounded to the nearest minute.

findings.title: Greek mu (μg) is misparsed as g, causing 1,000,000× overstatement of microgram doses
findings.description: The SQL cleaner keeps only [a–zµ] before matching. It includes the micro sign (µ, U+00B5) but not the Greek letter mu (μ, U+03BC). Labels using μg are common; 'μg' becomes 'g' after sanitization and maps to 1000 mg instead of 0.001 mg.
findings.evidence: REGEXP_REPLACE(..., '[^a-zµ]', '', 'g'); WHEN 'mcg'...'µg'...ELSE NULL. No explicit handling of 'μ' (Greek mu).
findings.recommendation: Add 'μ' to the retained charset and explicit 'μg' branch: REGEXP_REPLACE(..., '[^a-zµμ]', '', 'g'); treat 'μg' like 'mcg'/'µg'. Add unit-level regression tests for 'µg' and 'μg'.

findings.title: Supplement unit coverage is narrow and silently drops common real-world units (IU, mL, oz, capsules, mg/mL)
findings.description: unit_to_mg_factor returns NULL for many packaging units, removing those ingredients from pds.supplement_intake_by_compound and downstream totals. Vitamins A/D/E often labeled in IU; liquids in mL/fl-oz; forms like drops/capsules; concentrations like mg/mL normalize to 'mgml' and fall through.
findings.evidence: Function only maps mg, g, mcg/µg, kg. Docs note IU, oz, mL, fl-oz, drops, scoops, capsules become NULL; mg/mL collapses to mgml.
findings.recommendation: Expand mapping and/or stage a two-step normalization: (1) parse numeric + unit, (2) convert via per-compound IU↔mass crosswalk where defined (A, D, E), (3) support volume units with density when available, (4) preserve unknowns with a flag rather than NULL-drop, and (5) add a QA view listing unrecognized units so coverage gaps are visible.

findings.title: Ambiguous helper name: formatKcal expects kJ input, inviting accidental double-conversion
findings.description: formatKcal(kj) converts kJ→kcal and formats the result. The name suggests it formats an already-kcal value, increasing the risk that dietary kcal values are mistakenly divided by 4.184.
findings.evidence: export function formatKcal(kj: number | null | undefined): string { return `${Math.round(kjToKcal(kj))} kcal`; }
findings.recommendation: Rename to formatKjAsKcal or energyKjToKcalStr. Consider branded types (type Kilojoule = number & {__unit:'kJ'}) to catch misuse at compile time.

findings.title: Opaque select('*') increases semantic-conflation risk as schemas evolve
findings.description: Several queries use select('*'), pulling many similarly named fields (e.g., multiple HRV variants, calories from different sources). While current consumers appear disciplined, this pattern makes future conflation more likely as new columns are added.
findings.evidence: getHealthMatrix, getDailySummaries (pre-rename), getSleepData, etc. use select('*').
findings.recommendation: Prefer explicit column lists and typed interfaces per query, exposing only canonical fields needed by each consumer. Continue defensive renaming (as done for Garmin kcal) where overlap exists.

findings.title: Lack of branded unit types for seconds vs milliseconds and kJ vs kcal
findings.description: The code relies on naming conventions ('_seconds', '_milli') and comments. This is good practice but still allows unit mistakes at call sites that TypeScript can’t catch.
findings.evidence: Comments in queries.ts header and separate formatDuration/formatDurationMs helpers; no branded types to enforce units.
findings.recommendation: Introduce branded types (e.g., type Seconds = number & {__unit:'s'}; Milliseconds; Kilojoule; Kilocalorie) and annotate key APIs. This will surface unit mismatches at compile time.

findings.title: Distance formatter switches to meters for short distances, diverging from mile-oriented UI
findings.description: For distances <0.5 mi, the formatter shows rounded meters, which may feel inconsistent in a mile/lb/kcal UI. Not a unit error, but a presentation inconsistency.
findings.evidence: if (miles >= 0.5) return `${miles.toFixed(1)} mi`; else `${Math.round(meters)} m`.
findings.recommendation: Consider always showing miles (e.g., two decimals below 1 mi) to keep display units consistent, or make threshold configurable.
